newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS profits soar 67 percent in first half.
newsitem.headline: UBS profits soar 67 percent in first half.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), the country's biggest bank, said Tuesday group net profit surged 67.4 percent in the first half of 1997 to a record 1,856 million Swiss francs ($1.2 billion).
UBS said it was optimistic about performance for the full year, but conditions in the second half might not be as optimal as in the first six months.
"UBS assumes that its group profit for the full year will enable it to achieve its goal of a return on equity of over 12 percent," the group said.
The results were well-received on the Swiss stock exchange, although analysts said they were disappointed by flat trading income and a 20 percent rise in costs.
The UBS bearer shares rose at first, gaining 22 Swiss francs from the prior close to 1,690, and then fell to about 1,625 francs at midday as some investors took profits on what was seen as good news.
"Consolidated total assets increased by 77.4 billion ($50.8 billion) to 514.7 billion Swiss francs ($337.6 billion) at mid-year," UBS said in a letter to shareholders.

"A major factor behind our good results was the extraordinary robustness of the financial markets over the first six months, but our own structural re-engineering efforts also produced positive effects," UBS said.
